name: Tripwire
note: A basket is weights, not a promise. dayPct is the weighted mean of each leg's own last-day change; level is an index that starts at 100 at the first hourly snapshot and compounds from recorded per-leg values. No backtest: the history here was written by our own builds, one point per hour.

packages.name: ASX Steady
packages.thesis: The four things an Australian already owns, in the weights an Australian already owns them: two banks for the earnings that pay the dividend, BHP for the commodity cycle, and the index for everything else.
research: Banks are 50 points because Australian bank earnings move with the cash rate and housing credit, not with US tech sentiment — the two banks are half the basket and today's combined move is mostly theirs.
BHP at 25 is the commodity leg: iron ore and copper set its revenue, so this basket already contains a China-growth bet, sold to you as one stock.
The ASX 200 leg is 25 points of diversification for free — it holds the other three at slightly different weights, so a single-name blow-up cannot take the basket alone.
The honest risk is concentration by geography: four Australian exposures means a domestic recession is a basket-wide event, not one holding's problem.
packages.invalidates: A sustained fall in the cash rate that compresses bank net interest margins at the same time the iron ore price falls — both legs down for one macro reason, which is exactly when a 50-point bank weight stops diversifying.
packages.cadence: Checked hourly. A ±2.5% basket move in 24h is written to the hash chain and mailed with the constituent that contributed most.

packages.name: Global Core
packages.thesis: The two things people actually argue about — US earnings and the price of safety — in one number: 80 points of US equity in three shapes, against 20 points of gold as the thing that is not equity.
research: The index legs (50) and the single names (30) overlap by construction: Apple and Microsoft are among the largest weights inside both the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq, so real single-name exposure is higher than the 30 points shown. That is stated here rather than hidden behind a label.
Gold at 20 is the only holding whose price is not somebody's earnings — it moves on real yields and reserve demand, so it is the leg that can carry the basket on a day US equity does not.

FX is inside this basket whether you like it or not: three holdings quote in USD, so an Australian holder is also long USD against AUD. Weights act on returns, so this basket does not pretend the currency is neutral.
No bonds, no cash leg. The basket is always fully invested, which means its only defence is the 20-point gold position.
packages.invalidates: A US earnings recession with gold falling at the same time (real yields up, dollar up) — then 80 points of equity and the 20-point hedge go down together.
packages.cadence: Checked hourly. A ±3% basket move in 24h is written to the hash chain with the per-holding contribution, so the alert names the leg that moved.

packages.name: Momentum
packages.thesis: The highest-beta liquid things we can price for free, weighted so no single one can sink the basket: 60 points of crypto, 30 of high-beta US equity, 10 of crude.
research: Crypto is 60 points and correlates with itself: BTC and ETH have traded as one macro position for years, and SOL is a higher-amplitude version of the same trade. Three names, closer to one exposure — the weights say 60, the truth is nearer 60 as a single bet.
NVDA at 20 is the AI capex theme in single-name form: the same thesis as the Nasdaq leg of Global Core, at roughly twice the amplitude.

WTI at 10 is the only leg that is not a risk asset in the same way — crude spikes on supply shocks when equity is falling, so it is a partial hedge that pays no income and can gap on a single headline.
This basket is built to move. The ±6% alert is the feature, not a fault: expect it to trip most often, and expect drawdowns of a size the other two do not have.
packages.invalidates: A liquidity event where crypto, high-beta equity and crude fall on the same day — the 60-point crypto leg and the 30-point equity leg collapse into one position at the worst possible moment.
packages.cadence: Checked hourly. A ±6% basket move in 24h is written to the hash chain; because the legs are correlated, the alert fires early in a risk-off move rather than after it.
